full_judgment:
19. Admittedly the parties are second generation heirs of the purchaser of the landed property within the C.S. Plot No. 171 and 303. The plaintiff's claim that their predecessor Jomu Sheik is also a co-purchaser under the registered sub-kabala No. 766, dated 2.2.1937 Exhibit-ka. On the other hand the defendants flatly denied the fact that Jomu Sheik was the co-purchaser of the said sub-kabala Exhibit-ka and in support of their assertion they relies upon the original copy of the sub-kabala being No.766, dated 2.2.1937, Exhibit-ka, which shows the sole name of mokdom All Sheik as the purchaser. Therefore, the very burden lies on the plaintiff that Jomu sheik is a co-purchaser in the said registered sub-kabala as mandated under Section 103 of the evidence Act which runs as follows: 

 Burden of proof as to Particular Fact — The burden of proof as to any particular fact lies on that person who wishes the Court to believe in its existence, unless it is provided by any law that the proof of that fact shall lie on any particular person.
